correctness.rationale: The published weight formula gives \(p_{*,n}=W_*/(S_n+W_*)\). Under Gaussian shift, the likelihood ratios reduce exactly to lognormal weights. For \(0<\beta<2\), the standard-normal maximum law creates a strictly positive exponent gap \(\sqrt{2\beta}-\beta\), forcing \(W_*/S_n\to0\). For \(\beta>2\), an explicit fractional moment \(q=1-\sqrt{(\beta-2)/(2\beta)}\) and Markov's inequality make \(S_n\) polynomially smaller than \(W_*\) with high probability. At \(\delta_n=\sqrt{2\log n}\), truncation at \(W_i=n\) has exact mean \(1/2\), vanishing normalized variance, and a vanishing probability of any discarded term, so \(S_n/n\to1/2\); combining this with \(W_*/n=\exp(\delta_n Z_*)\) yields the Bernoulli critical limit. Boundary quantile logic is exact when calibration scores are finite. No finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The infinity atom is a built-in validity mechanism of weighted conformal prediction: when it exceeds the miscoverage budget, the method must return an infinite threshold. The theorem gives a sharp, interpretable overlap boundary for a canonical Gaussian shift, identifies the information scale \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}=\log n\), and resolves the exact critical behavior rather than merely showing instability. This is useful for diagnosing when additional source calibration data can or cannot prevent vacuous prediction under covariate shift, and it connects conformal abstention directly to a known importance-sampling overlap scale without reducing to a textbook restatement.
